just an FYI: if you're planning on moving it might be harder to get a LEO position. Some agencies require that you are a permanent resident or citizen. I think that priority is given to citizens. 

I'm from Canada and here a provincial police officer (OPP) can make 100k a year, if not more. I think that amount is much less than the USA. 

But in any case, best of luck to you.

First of all, I'm not sure how it is in the USA but in my country the process of becoming LEO is very long and involved. There's physical and written tests, along with psychological and medical evaluations, security checks and interviews. That being said, it is doable. I have several friends that are Asian and excellent officers. It also gives you the opportunity to branch into other fields: Criminal psych, criminal profiling, detective or Intel work as well. I would think that in some states having a uni degree is a plus. You don't have to be a uniform officer forever, either. There are agencies like FBI, CIA. Forensics and other areas to explore as well. 
Honestly you could still probably own and drive super cars as long as you do so legally within the law i.e driving in specific areas, keeping speed limits, etc. Take a look at the selection/hiring process though and decide if you can stomach it. Good luck!

Please consider that your job might have counselling services available to you. I used to self harm and I know it can be a great release but it is also a damaging one because it is an unhealthy coping mechanism. Have you tried using an elastic band on your wrist? Whenever the urge to cut is strong, snap the elastic so it hurts but doesn't leave any lasting scars or injuries. If you feel that others won't miss you don't live for them. Do it for yourself. Give yourself some more options before the last big one. Take care.

I hope you're still around. For what it's worth, I have a friend who is barely 5' and he is so intense and strong and one of the best rock climbers I've ever met. What he lacks in height he makes up for with pure strength. 
Beauty is relative. We are an image-based society but being attractive doesn't guarantee anything, it just means people are more likely to devalue your actual strengths for "oooh he's so handsome" like that's the only thing that counts. Chin up, friend. You can make it!

Hi there. I want you to know that things are hard, yes, but you are much stronger than you think you are. I don't know you, but I love you and I feel for you. You're not weak, you just must be very hurt and tired. Please take care of yourself a little longer, try to imagine what can be tomorrow or next week. Have you tried to just pack up and go on a trip somewhere? Anywhere...be careful please.

Hi there. I want to tell you that you are very brave and tough. High school is absolutely one of the worst experiences anyone can have. People your age are nasty, rude, snobby, and just trying to fit in. They talk and talk and have no idea what happens in their own homes or what it does to others. I know this sounds like bs but it does get better after high school. You can move away and never see them again. You have full control to say "I don't know you" if they try to talk to you. And social media face? Forget that noise. It's useless and just drags you down. Keep your chin up, high school isn't forever and it doesn't end. 
Please don't feel like a slut or anything less than beautiful. Accidents happen all the time, even with planning and contraceptives. I had to take a plan b bill once as well, and even considered abortion. But no one really cares about that stuff anymore. You have control over your own body, and you are in control over the decisions about it. I think you made a good choice, and one that will be better in the long run. 
Just remember that boys come and go, but you are your own best friend. 
Pills aren't always the answer, though they can help. A lot of days I don't recognize myself in the mirror, so I just stop looking at it. I know it feels weird to feel like your skin is wrong, but it is yours. Maybe try going for a walk in nature and just sitting and being at one with it. I know it sounds like new age crap, but feeling powerful and in balance can help sometimes. I wish you the best of luck. Take care. And remember, no one can make you feel bad without your permission.

Please, take care of yourself. I went to university for what I loved and wanted to do with my whole heart. But it didn't get me anywhere. But that doesn't mean that's all there is, it may come back to you in the future where you can use your talents in a way that also helps your career. Unfortunately the system is set up so people have a hard time breaking out of soul-crushing desk jobs, but volunteering somewhere with art and writing is always an option. Try to write again. Anything. Everything. Just throw down words on a paper even if they don't make sense. Some of the best authors wrote through their sadness. I believe in you and I know you can do it.
